liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Reviewer considers this the sharpest Dark Star ever; Dark Star is relatively short but a keeper [15][19][21]
- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Morning Dew especially passionate; By I'm A King Bee and Morning Dew, the band reaches a peak, driven by Kreutzmann's rhythms [15][17]
- **Hard To Handle** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls this the best Hard To Handle they have heard, and the second set strong overall; Reviewer calls this the best Hard To Handle ever, plus a tight blues jam with an incredible build-up [18][22]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Reviewer finds the Bird Song sweet [19]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Rhythms build in intensity like a locomotive, with Kreutzmann standing out; this version appears on the 1971 self-titled album [11]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): The missing Wharf Rat was released on the four-disc Ladies and Gentlemen set from the Fillmore East [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **Workingman's Blues**: rare: 14 archived performances [23]
- **Superman**: rare: 10 archived performances [23]
- **Truck Drivin' Man**: rare: 14 archived performances [23]
- **Runnin' Back To You**: rare: 4 archived performances [23]
- **Down In The Boondocks**: rare: 3 archived performances [23]
- **Garden Of Eden**: rare: 3 archived performances [23]
- **Glendale Train**: rare: 13 archived performances [23]
- **Sailing Song**: rare: 3 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd71-04-28.sbd.murphy.2248.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 42 songs; 270 min; rated 4.88/5 by 25 [1]. Said about its sound: Some popping on the tape during the New Riders' performance of The Weight; otherwise the recording is strong; The mix is almost perfect, according to the reviewer; Reviewer calls the sound unbelievable [13][18][21]
- **gd1971-04-28.sbd.kaplan-fink.11257.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 204 min [9]
- **gd1971-04-28.sbd.frisco.32862.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 203 min [10]
- **gd1971-04-28.sbd.unknown.4332.shnf**: soundboard; 42 songs; 270 min [2]

## Around the show

- An attendee says the New Riders set opened the show and is worth hearing for the full feel of the night [20]
- Bill Graham's introduction precedes Truckin' on the tape [9]
- Tom Constanten plays on the stretch from Dark Star through Not Fade Away [10]
- Reviewer prefers this night over 4/29 as the trippier of the final two Fillmore shows, though both have strong versions of the same songs [11]
- Reviewer rates this the best night of the Fillmore run, with both the New Riders and the Dead on fire [16]
- The setlist resembles many other shows of the era, yet this one has a distinctive energy [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-04-28.sbd.murphy.2248.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bob Murphy; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Second half of The Other One and Wharf Rat reportedly fell in a reel flip; the reel was supposedly hidden in a closet; Master from a Bob Murphy tape: MSR, then a reel after Bird Song, to Alesis Masterlink, then CD-R [1][15]
- **gd1971-04-28.sbd.kaplan-fink.11257.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Seth Kaplan and Alan Fink; source: Truckin'through Bird Song 02:07.38: MSR>Reel>Alesis Masterlink>CDR Bird Song 02:08.70 through end of show: MSR 7 inch(7.5 ips)Revox A 77>Alesis Masterlink>CDR… [9]. Also: Extracted by Seth Kaplan; Bird Song splice and Other One from 8:47 patched from other sources, including Skull & Roses; Bertha has a cut around 5:08, likely a reel flip, smoothed with a crossfade [9]
- **gd1971-04-28.sbd.frisco.32862.shnf**: transferred by refined, patched, retracked and SHN'ed by Chris Frisco at the Frisco Refinery, April 28, 2004.; source: MR>R>CDR [10]. Also: Several sources were synced to another soundboard; 21 glitches were repaired by repositioning sectors without deleting audio [10]
- **gd1971-04-28.sbd.unknown.4332.shnf**: transferred by Unknown; source: Workin' Man Blues through the cut in Bird Song: MR>R>CDR the cut in Bird Song through the end: MR>CDR [2]
